summary: Planning / contract analysis only (phase 149O.20L.7O.3W.1R.2B.1R.1.1R.21). Phase-entry SHA ced1b934. Re-derived N-16-3 from primary source (PBRD-001 v2.1 section 12 verbatim; RDGO-001 v3.1; PBPA-001; RE No-Go Registry schema 1.1; permission_broker_foundation.py ExecutionDisabledRule / _compose / _structural_request_failure / RuntimeDispatchRequestFacts / _valid_runtime_dispatch_request / _RUNTIME_DISPATCH_REQUEST_SEAL; runtime_dispatch_permission.py build_runtime_dispatch_permission_broker_request; .1R.16 sections 7/18/19/20/30/33/35/36.2; the .1R.19R.1 canonical report), not from phase summaries. CENTRAL QUESTION ANSWERED (frozen): a future local-CLI runtime_dispatch request becomes Permission-Broker ELIGIBLE (POL-005 does not categorically preclude ordinary PB evaluation) ONLY via a single TRUSTED-DERIVED execution profile RUNTIME_DISPATCH_LOCAL_CLI_V1 that is not within POL-005's historical hard-block domain, governed by a dedicated conjunctive policy POL-013 whose most permissive output is not-triggered -- it never emits ALLOW, never HUMAN_REVIEW, never suppresses another policy; any of the 21 profile predicates failing -> POL-005 retains its hard-DENY match AND POL-013 returns DENY (narrow_local_cli_dispatch_profile_incomplete). SELECTED ARCHITECTURE: Option C + D. Option B REJECTED -- _compose iterates (DENY, HUMAN_REVIEW) and returns the first category with any triggered rule; no specificity tier / weight / override channel, so a higher-specificity ALLOW cannot overcome a POL-005 DENY (code-proven); PBRD sections 9/12 also forbid weakening precedence. Option A inferior (POL-005 semantics become taxonomy-dependent). Option E rejected (rule is contract-expressible now, ships unsatisfiable). CURRENT POL-005 (re-derived, not paraphrased): triggered exactly when request.simulation_only is False; then an unconditional DENY (NG-025 / INV-001 / COMP-002) for every action_type and execution_class; universally applicable (no applicable_execution_classes -> None -> universal per PBPA-REQ-019); never HUMAN_REVIEW / ALLOW; no exception channel; absolute under _compose's DENY > HUMAN_REVIEW > ALLOW. The modeled future Slice-C PB request (14-fact sealed runtime_dispatch / execution_class=adapter / simulation_only=false / approval_present=true) -> DENY, causing_policy_ids=(POL-005,), matched_no_go_ids=(NG-025,) TODAY -- correct and required to remain so for every request outside the full narrow profile. PBRD-001 section 12 mandates the SHAPE of the rule (a narrowly scoped eligibility rule for the exact local-CLI runtime_dispatch profile; not deletion of POL-005, not a universal non-simulation bypass, not an inference that simulation_only=false is itself permission; every non-eligible non-simulation request remains denied) but does not define it -- N-16-3 authors it. (.1R.16 section 35 row 13's 'item 4 of the eleven' is an imprecise cross-reference; item 4 is the no-precedence-weakening CONSTRAINT, the rule itself is the section 12 closing mandate paragraph -- non-blocking; N-16-3 scope unchanged.) TARGET PROFILE RUNTIME_DISPATCH_LOCAL_CLI_V1 -- 21 trusted predicates: runtime_dispatch/adapter; transport_type=local_cli const; network_requirement=false MANDATORY; no credential/secret/provider/model field MANDATORY; no shell/command string; adapter_descriptor_binding carrying a resolvable canonical supply-chain admission binding of class local_fixed_argv (N-16-6); fixed argv from the admitted descriptor; trusted env allowlist; repo-scoped cwd; bounded resource/time-limit containment-profile references; human_authority_binding = valid RIHAC-001 v2.0 validated-authority projection for the exact invocation_id with a REAL (non-NON_REAL) assurance verdict (N-16-5); coordinator-minted attempt_id + idempotency_key; one exact runtime_target_id (no alias/fallback); digest-bound filesystem_scope_ref; the Slice-B durable dispatch-attempt lifecycle wired; a derived non-caller profile_classification marker set ONLY by the sealed trusted request builder from the other predicates. ANTI-BYPASS (load-bearing): every authority-bearing predicate is Caller-controllable? = No; the classification is trusted-derived, not caller-declared, at every predicate -- RuntimeDispatchRequestFacts is constructible only behind _RUNTIME_DISPATCH_REQUEST_SEAL; the generic build_permission_broker_request raises runtime_dispatch_requires_trusted_builder; _valid_runtime_dispatch_request fails closed on a missing seal / execution_class != adapter / network_requirement is not False / authority inconsistency; caller approval_present / attempt_id / idempotency_key are construction-time rejections (PBRD section 15); a fabricated adapter_id has no admission record (N-16-6) -> POL-013 DENY; Gate 8 re-hashes the executable; the PB decision expires on any request change (PBRD section 10). The sealed builder + const transport shipped in .1R.13 already provide the trusted-derivation substrate. SEMANTIC WALLS all verified against current source: human approval != PB permission != Runtime Enforcement capability != runtime execution availability != external effect; POL-005 eligibility != blanket execution permission. Human approval is ONE predicate among twenty-one, consumed once at Gate 9, never a policy override; 'if human_approved: ignore POL-005' and 'trusted principal -> ALLOW' explicitly rejected (_compose has no channel by which any input flips a DENY). ELIGIBILITY != ALLOW: a ..._V1 request that clears POL-005 and POL-013 is still subject to POL-001/003/004/006/007 and the full DENY > HUMAN_REVIEW > ALLOW composition -- POL-004 still emits HUMAN_REVIEW (dominates ALLOW) if approval absent; the ALLOW branch of _compose is reached only when no rule triggered DENY or HUMAN_REVIEW; the narrow profile never directly returns ALLOW by classification. DEFAULT-DENY OUTSIDE THE EXACT PROFILE: any missing predicate / unknown-state / malformed binding / unsupported adapter class / broader effect profile -> POL-005 DENY AND POL-013 DENY; no fuzzy matching; profile_classification must be the exact literal RUNTIME_DISPATCH_LOCAL_CLI_V1. CONCEPTUAL DELTAS (no contract or production edit this phase): PBRD-001 new section 12a spelling out the rule -- MINOR (-> v2.2), defines the rule section 12 already mandated, adds no request fact, changes no precedence, invalidates no old valid request. POL-005 -- canonical-statement VERSIONED AMENDMENT; POL-005 RETAINS ITS ID for audit-trail continuity; match domain gains exactly one trusted-derived carve-out; the policy-semantics change is MAJOR-class and carried with an explicit migration note + independent verification, but WITHOUT a new policy ID and WITHOUT deleting POL-005 (section 12 forbids deletion). POL-013 -- new additive conjunctive policy (applicable only to runtime_dispatch/adapter; never emits ALLOW). PB request schema -- two additive INTERNAL, NON-CALLER fields: RuntimeDispatchRequestFacts.profile_classification (derived by the trusted builder) and RuntimeDispatchAdapterDescriptorBinding.admission_record_digest / admission_class (from N-16-6's admitted-descriptor preflight); both inside the PBRD section 5 canonical request digest and transitively consumption.json record_digest; no caller-visible field added; existing callers leave runtime_dispatch_context = None and are unaffected. RE No-Go Registry -- NG-025 canonical-statement annotation only (schema unchanged). RDGO-001 / RIHAC / RIASC / HPAC / RPAC / PBPA -- no change. POLICY PRECEDENCE re-derived: DENY > HUMAN_REVIEW > ALLOW, fail-closed, no specificity tier / weight / override; POL-005 not triggering for ..._V1 removes one DENY contributor, does not add an ALLOW, does not change the algorithm; POL-013 only ever contributes nothing (pass) or a DENY (fail); section 12 item 4 (no precedence weakening) satisfied by construction. HARD NO-GO PRESERVATION: POL-001/003/004/006/007, the _valid_runtime_dispatch_request structural failure path, RE-NOGO-001..017, and POL-005-for-every-non-..._V1-non-simulation-request all still dominate. BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY: no legacy caller becomes eligible accidentally (profile_classification == '' -> POL-005 DENYs as today); provider/network/credential requests stay blocked; the dry adapter_invocation / simulation_only=true path untouched; stored /2.0 and /2.1 records unaffected. GATE RELATIONSHIPS: Gate 5 validates human authority and MUST NOT decide POL eligibility; Gate 6 is the sole PB policy owner (N-16-3 belongs here entirely); PB eligibility MUST NOT imply a Gate-7 ALLOW (Gate 7 re-evaluates independently); containment (Gate 8) and final effect-state read-back (Gate 10) remain downstream; even a future PB ALLOW + RE ALLOW produces NO external effect while EXECUTION_AVAILABILITY == unavailable (RDGO section 11 item 5). POSITIVE-PATH STRUCTURAL REACHABILITY: after .1R.22 alone production CANNOT produce a RUNTIME_DISPATCH_LOCAL_CLI_V1 PB ALLOW -- N-16-6 (no admission store), N-16-5 (Gate 5 hard-stops NON_REAL), N-16-7 (capability unavailable) each independently keep the profile incomplete; .1R.22 may ship a NON-admitting fail-closed stub; this is the safer contract-consistent outcome. N-16-4..7 DEPENDENCY ORDERING (frozen): N-16-3 -> N-16-4 (real positive single-attempt Runtime Enforcement gate) -> N-16-5 (real FIDO2 / WebAuthn / CTAP + protected human-approval UI) -> N-16-6 (RPAC-REQ-095 fixed-argv external-executable adapter + supply-chain admission) -> N-16-7 (runtime capability enablement Observed -> Approved/Executable, STRICTLY LAST); adjudicated N-16-4 before N-16-5 (structural positive RE path can be verified while real HPAC is unreachable, lower-risk, no hardware dependency); each of N-16-4..7 is its own explicitly authorized implementation + IV pair; Slice C / D keep no phase ID. NO src/pcae change, NO normative contract change, NO POL-005 change, NO POL-013 module, NO RuntimeDispatchRequestFacts field, NO trusted-builder change, NO adapter call site; runtime remains not_implemented / Observed / observe / unavailable; POL-005 unchanged and still hard DENY.
